To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new series of coumarin‐based triazolothiadizine hybrid compounds were designed and synthesized.

we synthesized a new series of coumarin‐triazolothiazine hybrids, evaluated for their biological activities, and found that compounds 5j, 5h and 5i were the most active against ALP, L. major and H‐157 cells respectively.
we have designed and synthesized a series of novel coumarin–1,2,3,4‐trisubstituted triazolothiadizine hybrids, and the most potent compounds were evaluated as inhibitors of ALP and anticancer agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of a new class of coumarin‐triazolothiazine hybrids, which are potent ALP inhibitors.
the development of a new class of coumarin‐triazolothiazine hybrids, which are endowed with potent ALP inhibitory, anticancer, and antileishmanial activities.
the design and synthesis of a novel class of coumarin‐triazolothiazine hybrids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesized coumarin–1,2,3‐triazolothiazine hybrids are potential candidates for further development as potent inhibitors of alkaline phosphatases, antileishmanials, and anticancer agents.
the synthesized coumarin–thiadiazine hybrid molecules are promising candidates for the development of anticancer, antileishmanial, and anti‐ALP agents.

the coumarin–1,2,3‐triazol‐5‐yl‐1,2‐thiazole‐3‐carboxylate hybrid system is a promising scaffold for the design and development of novel anticancer agents with potent ALP inhibition and antileishmanial activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synthesized hybrid coumarin–1,2,3‐triazole derivatives are potent inhibitors of ALPs and also possess antileishmanial and anticancer potential.

the coumarin‐based compounds have shown promising results in the inhibition of ALP, anticancer, and antileishmanial activities, which may pave the way for the development of novel anticancer and anti‐Leishmania agents.

the newly synthesized coumarin–1,2,3‐triazolo[4,5‐b]pyridine‐5‐carbothioamide derivatives (5a–c) were found to be more effective against Leishmania and ALP than the standard drugs (miltefosine and alendronate) used in this study, whereas compounds 5i and 5j showed better anticancer activity than the standard compounds vincristine and cis‐platin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular docking study can be used as a complementary tool in the design and development of new inhibitors of ALP.
the synthesized compounds can be used as potential ALP inhibitors and anticancer/antileishmanial agents.
the synthesized coumarin–tri‐azole hybrids are potent ALP inhibitors, which may serve as potential lead compounds for the treatment of ALP related diseases such as cancer and leishmaniasis.
